items.title: Flames’ Devin Cooley exits vs. Oilers with lower-body injury
items.body: Calgary Flames goaltender Devin Cooley was replaced by Dustin Wolf after the first period following a hard bump from Edmonton Oilers forward Colton Dach. Dach crashed into Cooley with 12 seconds remaining in the opening 20 minutes and received a two-minute penalty for goaltender interference. Cooley remained in for the final 12 seconds but was not on the bench to start the second. He was then ruled out for the remainder of the game with a lower-body injury, the team announced. The injury interrupted Cooley's run of hot play. The 29-year-old had allowed just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four games entering play Wednesday, good for a .955 save percentage. Cooley had allowed one goal on nine shots through 20 minutes against the Oilers. However, it isn't just Cooley's strong performance that's turned heads lately. The netminder has drawn attention for his viral post-game interviews, including saying that he "felt nothing" while playing well and sharing that off the ice "he's reading with his rabbit and not thinking about much." Flames forward Brennan Othmann was also ruled out for the remainder of the game with an upper-body injury after fighting Oilers defenceman Ty Emberson in the first period.

items.body: Register Login Senators Searching For Scoring Help By Brian La Rose | at October 28, 2026 9:00 pm The Senators find themselves in 21st place in terms of goals scored per game in the early going this season. While Plan A is always to try to have someone come up from the minors and help give a team a lift when they’re struggling, there isn’t a viable player to take that role in Ottawa. William Eklund , who was counted on to be a key offensive pickup this summer, suffered a torn tendon in his ankle in the fourth game of the season. He’s out until at least January, meaning that there isn’t much internal help coming for a while. Accordingly, Postmedia’s Bruce Garrioch reports that GM Steve Staios has started calling around to see what options might be out there to try to add to his forward group. It’s far from the first time that the Sens have looked to see what’s out there but most of their in-season moves in the past have been on the incremental side of things. Given that the season is still relatively young, those are realistically the only options that are available at the moment. Teams are still assessing what they have and need, meaning that trades of significance aren’t likely on that horizon. Garrioch suggests Chicago’s Teuvo Teravainen as someone who could be in play. He’s on an expiring $5.4MM contract and has seen his ice time cut early on this year. Oilers’ McDavid sets NHL record with 13-game season-opening assist streak
items.body: Connor McDavid is red-hot to start the season, and the records are starting to pile up. With an assist in the first period against the Calgary Flames on Wednesday, the Edmonton Oilers captain set an NHL record for the longest season-opening assist streak. McDavid now has at least one assist in each of Edmonton's first 13 games this season, which breaks the previous record of 12 season-opening games held by Wayne Gretzky (1982-83), Ken Linseman (1985-86) and Sebastian Aho (2018-19). Wednesday's apple brought McDavid's point total to a ridiculous 35 points (12 goals, 27 assists) in just 13 games. He also has 33 points in the month of October, which tied Gretzky (33 in 1986) for the third-most points in a single October in NHL history. McDavid's hot start has helped the Oilers to an 8-2-2 start this season.

items.body: Wild GM says ‘nothing really to talk about right now’ on deal for defenseman, who can be free agent after season Minnesota Wild general manager Bill Guerin said Wednesday he has not spoken with representatives for defenseman Quinn Hughes “in a long time” with the 2024 Norris Trophy winner in the final season of his contract. The 27-year-old has been eligible to sign a new contract with the Wild since July 1 and can become an unrestricted free agent on July 1, 2027. He signed a six-year, $47.1 million contract ($7.85 million average annual value) with the Vancouver Canucks on Oct. 3, 2021. “To be quite honest with you I have not talked to them about this in a long time,” Guerin said. “To be honest with you there’s nothing really to talk about right now. What am I going to do, like, go and (say), ‘Please, please, please, please’? This is a unique situation, I think Quinn needs to wrap his head around a couple things, and I don’t think anything’s changed. I’m being honest with you. “Right now I’m focused on our team. … Quinn’s situation will resolve itself at some point in time, and like I said, this does not keep me awake at night. Yes I do think about it, but it’s not something that I’m going to let affect anything else I do. He’s going to take his time with it, and that’s it.” Hughes has 18 points (three goals, 15 assists) in 14 games this season, second among NHL defensemen and second on the Wild behind forward Kirill Kaprizov (23 points; 14 goals, nine assists). He reached 500 career points Sunday in a 4-2 win against the Canucks in his 520th NHL game, becoming the seventh fastest defenseman all-time -- and second fastest American defenseman after Brian Leetch (496 games) -- to reach the milestone. The 34 year old originally signed a short-term contract with HC Lugano that was set to expire at the end of October. Switzerland, and a championship, must have made a warm impression, as Shore went on to join HC Ambri-Piotta for the start of the 2022-23 season. He made another mid-season move that year, heading to HV71 in Sweden’s SHL. Shore stayed in the SHL – splitting his time between HV71 and Linkoping HC – until the end of the 2025-26 season. items.summary: Despite Zach Hyman heading to the injured reserve, the Edmonton Oilers are getting two key members of their lineup back.
items.body: Despite Zach Hyman heading to the injured reserve, the Edmonton Oilers are getting two key members of their lineup back. Centre Jason Dickinson and defenceman Mattias Ekholm are expected to return against the Calgary Flames on Wednesday. Dickinson has struggled with injuries this season, missing time on two separate occasions already. He's been sidelined since Oct. 15 with an undisclosed injury suffered in practice, and he also missed the first three games of the season with a foot injury. The 31-year-old has suited up in just three games, grabbing an assist while averaging 12:12 of ice time. He was activated from the injured reserve on Wednesday. Ekholm missed the last two games with a concussion suffered in last Thursday's win over the Carolina Hurricanes. He has one goal and two assists in 10 games. items.body: Register Login Capitals Activate Logan Thompson; Reassign Mitch Gibson By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 3:58 pm After returning as a regular to practice yesterday, the Washington Capitals will return their starting netminder to the active roster. According to beat reporter Sammi Silber , the Capitals activated netminder Logan Thompson from the injured reserve and assigned Mitch Gibson to the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Thompson has been on Washington’s injured reserve with a lower-body ailment since their October 20th matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Fortunately, the Capitals had only one game in the past week, limiting Thompson’s absence. Despite beating the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday, Washington likely wasn’t confident in Charlie Lindgren as the starter moving forward. The Capitals’ defense bailed him out for much of the game, limiting the Sabres to 21 shots on net through 63:42. Still, Lindgren stopped only 15 of those attempts, leading to a disappointing .857 SV% on the night. Now the Capitals can return to a netminder who has been on cruise control since joining the organization ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. This season, Thompson has earned a 4-3-0 record in seven starts with a .901 SV% and 2.90 GAA, including 1.9 Goals Saved Above Average. Throughout the past two years, Thompson has managed a dominant 62-27-12 record with a .911 SV% and 2.46 GAA, including two fourth-place finishes in Vezina Trophy voting. Meanwhile, Gibson returns to AHL Hershey without debuting in the NHL. He’s gotten off to a subpar start this season, splitting his first two appearances with an .881 SV% and 3.50 GAA.

items.title: McKenna unites with Matthews as Maple Leafs juggle lineup

items.body: “I’m sure there’ll be an opportunity at some point where we’re going to play together, and I’m sure it’ll be a lot of fun.” — Auston Matthews on Gavin McKenna , September 16 SEATTLE — It took until Game 15, but Gavin McKenna finally walked into the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ dressing room and saw his name to the left of Auston Matthews’ on the top line, along with Jack Roslovic. “When you see that, I think a little bit of a boost of confidence,” McKenna said Wednesday morning at Climate Pledge Arena, ahead of the Leafs’ game against the Seattle Kraken. “When you’re playing with two guys like that, you've got to make sure you're working. I want to make the most out of this opportunity, so I’m looking forward to it.” So is Leafs Nation, a fan base begging to see what magic Toronto’s two most recent first-overall draft picks can conjure in regular rotation. “Whenever he’s open, you want to find him in a spot because he's dangerous in all areas of the ice. So, you want to get him the puck,” McKenna said of his new centreman. But remember, it was mentor Matthews who set up McKenna’s first-ever NHL goal three weeks ago, in an emotional comeback win over Nashville. “His playmaking is something. I didn’t really know how good he was at making those plays coming into the league. I think he's made a ton of nice plays not a lot of guys can make. So, when he’s got the puck on his stick, you've got to be ready as well,” McKenna noted. McKenna and Matthews sit beside each other on the road and have flashed power-play chemistry. But they’ve skated just 19:04 together five-on-five this season, outshooting the competition 11-4 and outscoring them 2-0. 32 Thoughts: The Podcast Hockey fans already know the name, but this is not the blog. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images A heavy amount of injury news in The Six. On Wednesday, the Toronto Maple Leafs announced that forward Kirill Marchenko is considered week-to-week with a lower-body injury. On top of that, the Maple Leafs revealed that forward Dakota Joshua has been recalled from his conditioning loan to the team’s American Hockey League franchise, the Toronto Marlies. Marchenko suffered a lower-body injury during Monday night’s loss to the Calgary Flames . During the second period, the 26-year-old fell awkwardly into the boards after receiving a hit from Flames forward Yegor Sharangovich. Marchenko trudged off the ice in pain, walked down the tunnel to the Leafs’ dressing room and didn’t return to the contest. Marchenko has been a solid addition to Toronto’s lineup since the Original Six franchise received him in a preseason blockbuster trade with the Columbus Blue Jackets . In 14 games thus far, he has posted six goals and 14 points. While the Leafs had to give up a young Matthew Knies to make the deal happen, early returns are positive for the Russian winger. In 307 career regular-season NHL games, Marchenko has collected 108 goals and 222 points. The Leafs had updates on a couple of other players who are on the shelf. Defenseman Chris Tanev remains out of action with an upper-body injury, but is considered day-to-day after returning to practice. items.summary: In Oliver Moore’s 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago’s offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal.
items.body: CHICAGO — In Oliver Moore 's 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago's offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal. In Moore's 71st game, he was all over the ice in a big win for the Blackhawks. That's how it's going at the moment in Chicago, where the team's youngest players are still learning on the job. Moore was a healthy scratch for Sunday’s 3-2 loss to Florida, but he returned to the lineup Tuesday night and played quite well in a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings. “I didn’t expect anything less,” coach Jeff Blashill said. “He actually was playing good hockey. I felt it was a moment where him and our team needed to make sure we learn these lessons about not beating ourselves. But he’s played good hockey, so it’s not like he went through a stretch where he hadn’t been playing well. He stepped right back in and did a good job.” Moore, a first-round pick in the 2023 draft, is a key figure for Chicago as it tries to find the other side of years of rebuilding. The 21-year-old Minnesota native signed a $21.25 million, five-year contract in September. Losers of eight of their first 12 games, the Blackhawks are looking for more offence once again. They are averaging 2.17 goals, ranking No. 31 in the NHL going into Wednesday's action. They averaged just 2.56 goals last season. Moore has elite speed and athleticism, but he is still working on finishing his scoring opportunities. He has two goals and one assist in 11 games after he had five goals and 14 assists in 51 games all of last season. Facing Montreal on Friday, he tried to make a backhand pass from the corner to Ryan Greene in the middle. It was intercepted by Owen Beck, who started a rush that led to Jake Evans' tying score in the first period of the Canadiens' 4-1 win.

Largely an AHL talent since turning pro, Crotty has bounced from the Tucson Roadrunners to the Iowa Wild before landing with the Senators. His most productive years were with the Roadrunners when he scored four goals and 26 points in 119 combined games during the 2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons. In the NHL, Crotty has served as an injury replacement, typically only when the other injury replacement is injured. Debuting with the Coyotes in the 2023-24 season, Crotty has skated in 11 games since, registering one assist with a -1 rating, averaging 12:34 of ice time per game. items.body: The price for Detroit’s Dylan Larkin, according to league sources, isn’t just exorbitant. “It should be,” said one Eastern Conference executive, granted anonymity to speak openly about another team’s business. “He’s been a No. 1 centre for almost all his time there, and that has its own price. But factor in his cap hit ($8.7M through 2031) in this landscape, and that’s worth a premium.” This conversation was playing out over text while the Canadiens were completing a win in Chicago under the watchful eyes of Red Wings assistant general manager Kris Draper, who’s surely been following them for no other reason than due diligence for a potential trade. He was there in Toronto for Game 1 between the Canadiens and Leafs, then in Montreal for Canadiens-Sharks Oct. 20, and once again in Chicago for Canadiens-Blackhawks last Friday. There were rumblings he was at the Heritage Classic in Winnipeg Sunday—though we didn’t see him there—but he was definitely at Enterprise Center for Canadiens-Blues Tuesday, and it’s not because he’s suddenly become a fan of either team. If all of this smacks as absurd to you because Larkin hasn’t officially listed Montreal as one of the cities he’s willing to waive his no-movement clause for, consider that there aren’t many—if any—teams on his list loaded with the type of assets the Canadiens have to offer for the player’s services. Still, that doesn’t mean they’re willing to meet the current price that’s been set for the 30-year-old’s services. “It’s not about to come down, either, with the Wings hanging around and winning games,” added our league executive, and he was right. After losing five of their first six—one in a shootout to Montreal and one in overtime to the New Jersey Devils—the Wings have won four of six for a respectable 5-4-3 record.

items.title: Where the NHL salary cap could soar to in the next three years
items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap is still going through a “smoothing” process as the league comes out of the pandemic-induced flat cap wanting to avoid a sudden jump. But as we get to the end of that process, how high could the upper limit climb? Frank Seravalli has the story.
items.body: At the very end of his Board of Governors’ media conference last month on the 101 st floor of 30 Hudson Yards in Manhattan, NHL commissioner Gary Bettman offered an unprompted forewarning on the future of hockey’s salary cap. “Somebody had asked about the cap going up,” Bettman jumped in. “Please keep in mind that the cap going up at the rate it’s going up, it’s still a function of recapturing where we’re supposed to be after years of a flat cap,” Bettman said. “That number continues to be [managed] as we try to create a smooth increase in cap and not drive everyone crazy by who happened to be a free agent in a year with a huge jump.” Bettman reminded that once the system recaptures it, which he estimated “it will take two more years give or take,” then the cap “will go up at the same rate as revenues grow.” Fortunately for Bettman and the NHL, revenue continues to climb at record rates. But that means the salary cap will require even more finessing to smooth out drastic increases – because the cap is being kept so artificially low this season that there is a pending explosion. According to projections run by Sportsnet , verified by multiple team, league and Players’ Association sources, the NHL’s salary cap ceiling could reach $150 million USD by 2029-30 – just three seasons from now. That is a whopping 44 per cent increase from this season’s ceiling of $104 million. The calculation is relatively simple and we can use crumbs of information from Bettman’s media availability. He said last month that this season’s projected revenue was “just north” of $8 billion, or $8 billion “and change” in “mixed currency” since the league’s teams earn revenue in American and Canadian dollars. Sources said the league internally has that projection at $7.1 billion USD plus $1 billion CA

items.summary:
Semyon Varlamov waited long enough.
Nearly two years since previously winning an NHL game, the 38-year-old goalie was mobbed by his New York Islanders teammates after their 4-3 shootout victory at the Nashville Predators on Tuesday, a celebration honoring Varlamov's long journey back to the League following double partial knee
items.body: Teammates, coaches thrilled for goalie, who calls it 'very special moment' Nearly two years since previously winning an NHL game, the 38-year-old goalie was mobbed by his New York Islanders teammates after their 4-3 shootout victory at the Nashville Predators on Tuesday, a celebration honoring Varlamov's long journey back to the League following double partial knee replacements. It was Varlamov's first win since Nov. 14, 2024, when he made 24 saves in a 5-2 victory at the Vancouver Canucks. It's been so long, only seven skaters from that night were in the lineup in Nashville. But after the medical marvel proved to Islanders brass in training camp he was physically able to return to the NHL, Varlamov is back. "It's an amazing feeling, a very special moment," Varlamov told reporters after the game, following his 20-save performance. "A year ago, to be honest with you, I didn't see this coming. It was such a grind, like the last two years, to get to this point when you have the opportunity to play and then compete at the highest level in the world. I mean, I'm very thankful for this opportunity." Perhaps it was fitting Barry Trotz was on hand at Bridgestone Arena, the former Islanders coach now a senior adviser with the Predators, the team he coached from its inception in 1998 until leaving for the Washington Capitals in 2014. He won his first Stanley Cup championship four years later before helping turn the Islanders around during a four-season run (2018-22) that was highlighted by back-to-back trips to the third round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs. Varlamov won 18 postseason games during those runs in 2020 and 2021. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images Very rarely does a superstar player’s stat line cause a double take. After all, these players are the best of the best. We should be accustomed to seeing them put up crazy numbers every season. Heck, Connor McDavid is averaging almost three points a game, and no one is batting an eye because it’s not out of the realm of possibility for a player of his caliber. But Kirill Kaprizov’s start to the season might raise an eyebrow or two. If you told me that, one eighth into the season, he’d be leading the league in goal scoring, I wouldn’t be surprised. He’s an incredibly talented player, and he’s playing alongside Matt Boldy and Quinn Hughes. That’s a recipe for success, so an increase in goal scoring isn’t all that surprising. But 14 goals in 14 games is a stat line that raises a few more questions. First off, it’s very rare for a player to average a goal per game in the NHL, at least since the league’s early years. According to NHL.com, only 31 players have averaged a goal-per-game pace or higher in a season with a minimum of 18 games played (the fewest games ever played in an NHL regular season, occurring in 1918-19). Twenty-four of those instances happened in the first seven seasons of the league, when teams consistently averaged four-plus goals per game. It was the 42nd of 46 saves that Fowler would make, his airtight goaltending in Montreal's 2-0 victory giving him the Canadiens record for most saves in a game by a rookie. Technically, Esposito wasn't yet a rookie, winning the Calder Trophy with the 1969-70 Chicago Black Hawks. items.title: Oilers place Zach Hyman on injured reserve
items.summary: Hyman has one goal in six games with the Oilers in 2026-27. He has already missed six games due to injury.
items.body: Hyman, 34, left Monday’s game against the Detroit Red Wings in the second period after he took a hit from Red Wings’ defenseman Andreas Englund. He appeared to hit his head against the glass and fell to the ice, then required help to the dressing room from the Oilers’ training staff. He finished the night with two shots on goal in 8:25 of ice time. Hyman’s injury comes soon after he missed more than two weeks due to an injury sustained during Edmonton’s regular-season opener against the Vancouver Canucks on Sept. 29. He missed six games then returned to the lineup Oct. 17 against the Utah Mammoth . Through six games, Hyman has one goal and is averaging 17:56 of ice time. Now in his 12th NHL season, the Toronto native has 262 goals and 234 assists for 496 points in 717 regular-season games with the Oilers and Toronto Maple Leafs . He scored a career-high 54 goals with Edmonton in 2023-24. Hyman, a 2010 fifth-round pick for the Florida Panthers , also has 42 goals and 33 assists for 75 points in 106 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He was part of the Oilers’ back-to-back Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025, and scored a league-leading 16 goals during the postseason in 2024. Edmonton is 8-2-2 with 18 points through their first 12 games of 2026-27. Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard make up three of the NHL’s top-five point leaders going into Wednesday night, with McDavid having 34 in just 12 games.

items.summary: Zach Hyman is heading back to the injured reserve.
items.body: The Edmonton Oilers forward has been placed on IR with a "stiff neck," head coach Mike Babcock told reporters on Wednesday. Hyman suffered the injury in Monday's loss to the Detroit Red Wings when he took a hit from Andreas Englund. He hit his head hard on the glass and appeared dazed. He required assistance to leave the ice. Hyman was in just his fifth game back after missing over two weeks with an upper-body injury he suffered in the Oilers' pre-season finale. Despite the pre-season injury, Hyman did play in the regular-season opener before going on IR. The 34-year-old has one goal in six games played this season.

items.title: Charlie Jacobs to take over from father as Bruins’ governor
items.summary: Charlie takes the reins from his dad, Jeremy, continuing the family legacy that spans over a half-century.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images A huge change in operations in New England. On Wednesday, the Boston Bruins announced that CEO Charlie Jacobs is going to take over as the team’s governor from his father, Jeremy M. Jacobs, who held the role for 51 years. Charlie will represent the club on the NHL’s Board of Governors. “It is a tremendous honor to step into the role as governor of the Boston Bruins,” the younger Jacobs said in a release. “Representing the team that has been part of my family for the past 51 years. I step into this role with the goal of continuing to build upon the incredible legacy and the impact that my dad has had on this franchise and the NHL over his five decades of leadership. Dad will continue to serve as my mentor and sounding board through this next era of the Bruins. I am looking forward to partnering with the NHL Board of Governors Chairman Ted Leonsis, Vice Chair Murray Edwards, our peers, and Commissioner Bettman on continuing to grow this beautiful game that we all love.” The move to promote Charlie comes as Jeremy is starting to move out of the spotlight. Last month, he stepped down as Chairman of the league’s board of governors, and Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis was unanimously voted in as the new chair. Charlie has been part of the organization since 2000, when he was named the Bruins’ alternate governor. He also serves as the CEO of Delaware North, a multinational food service and hospitality company, which has ownership shares of NESN, the Bruins’ local broadcaster.

items.body: Hockey Hall of Famer, New Jersey exec thrilled to land goalie in trade with Jets Martin Brodeur believed the New Jersey Devils reached the point where a move for an elite goaltender like Connor Hellebuyck wasn't just warranted. It was necessary. New Jersey's core players are entering or firmly established in the prime of their careers. Brodeur, its executive vice president of hockey operations, said acquiring the 33-year-old goalie reflects the Devils' commitment to take the next step. "It's like the window of winning," Brodeur said in an interview with NHL Network on Tuesday. "Our guys are there. You look at Nico Hischier (27 years old), Jack Hughes (25), Jesper Bratt (28), Timo Meier (30), they're (mostly) all in their late 20s, with Jack a little younger. But I think it was time for us to make a move like that. (General manager) Sunny (Mehta) pulled it off, and it's awesome." Brodeur understands perhaps better than anyone what Hellebuyck provides -- a proven No. 1 goalie who embraces the responsibility that comes with being one of the most important players on the team. Hellebuyck made 17 saves Tuesday for his first victory with New Jersey, a 5-1 win at the Dallas Stars in his first NHL game since April 13, four days after being acquired in a trade with the Winnipeg Jets for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad , goalie Nico Daws , the rights to unsigned draft choice Alexander Command , the Devils' own second-round pick in the 2029 NHL Draft and their seventh-round selection in the 2027 NHL Draft. Brodeur played 1,266 games during his 22-season NHL career, including 1,259 with New Jersey, and won the Vezina Trophy as the League's best goalie four times (2003, 2004, 2007, 2008) and the Stanley Cup three times (1995, 2000, 2003). items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck wasn’t the only superstar stopper to change teams in the past 25 years.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Congratulations to Connor Hellebuyck. After a public trade request and holdout, the star goaltender finally escaped the wintry wasteland of Winnipeg to reach the sunny climes of… Newark, New Jersey? OK, Hellebuyck’s move from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils may not have gotten him the palm trees and tax breaks that have been so en vogue for NHL players lately, but the 33-year old might just be the final piece for a talented young team that has been trying to get over the proverbial hump for years now. Will the deal put the Devils over the top? Will it help nourish a successful new era for the Jets? Well, there’s already been sharp analysis on the trade as we still sit in its aftershock, but truly, none of us can see the future, and only time will give us a definitive answer. In the meantime, maybe the best we can do, as a wise mandrill once said, is learn from the past. items.title: Kapanen picking up speed with some of NHL’s fastest skating for Oilers
items.summary: EDMONTON -- Kasperi Kapanen can fly and has the numbers to prove it.
items.body: Fourth in NHL in bursts over 22 mph, including highest maximum by a forward EDMONTON -- Kasperi Kapanen can fly and has the numbers to prove it. The Edmonton Oilers right wing posted the fastest maximum skating speed of any NHL forward this season at 24.05 miles per hour in a 3-1 win at the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 10, per NHL EDGE stats . Only St. Louis Blues defenseman Philip Broberg has clocked faster with a burst of 24.26 mph in a 5-2 loss at the Nashville Predators on Oct. 17. “If I’m up there, that means I’m still a decent skater,” Kapanen said Tuesday. “Skating has always, since I started playing hockey, something that I was good at. I was always one of the fastest ones out there. But even though it is your strength, I love working at it as well and trying to be better.” Kapanen will get another chance to display his speed when the Oilers host the Calgary Flames at Rogers Place on Wednesday (8:30 p.m. ET; Prime). Kapanen’s top speed this season is the fastest by an NHL forward since Nathan MacKinnon of the Colorado Avalanche topped out at 24.78 mph in a 3-2 loss against the Blues on April 5 last season. Kapanen has nine bursts over 22 mph this season, which is tied with New York Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer for fourth, behind teammate Connor McDavid (26), MacKinnon (24) and Toronto Maple Leafs forward Jack Roslovic (10). “Playing with guys like ‘Davo’ (McDavid) it does inspire me in a way to work on my skating,” Kapanen said. “I know I’m never going to keep up with him, but you can try and learn things, so it’s always going to be a big factor for me.” McDavid is considered one of the fastest skaters in NHL history, and he doesn’t slow down all that much when he has the puck. items.summary: Thanks to an OT snipe from Filip Hronek and some late-game heroics from Jonathan Lekkerimaki, the Canucks finally found some good vibes. Courtney Jacobsen has the takeaways from Tuesday’s slump-busting win.
items.body: In the midst of a prolonged losing streak, the Vancouver Canucks were in desperate need of some good vibes. With just one win in the month of October, it was getting understandably difficult for the Canucks to maintain some positivity about what they're building towards. And when Quinn Hughes and the Minnesota Wild handed the Canucks their 10th straight loss Sunday, morale was at an all-time low. But Tuesday night against the Anaheim Ducks, the Canucks clawed back from an early deficit, earning an impressive 6-5 victory to get finally back into the win column thanks to an overtime snipe from Filip Hronek and some late-game heroics from Jonathan Lekkerimaki. It was a win that took a fair bit of resilience from a dejected Vancouver squad. For much of the night in Southern California, the Canucks looked to be headed to a familiar fate. A three-goal second period from the Ducks put the Canucks into a 4-1 hole that seemed, at times, insurmountable. That was Batherson's eighth point in five games, and it's the sixth game in a row the Golden Knights have allowed a power-play goal. items.title: Islanders’ Schaefer becomes first player post-lockout to play all five minutes of overtime
items.summary: The 19-year-old defenseman finished the game with over 32 minutes of ice time.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images New York Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer exceeded all expectations in his rookie campaign last season. Now, just a dozen games into his sophomore season, he’s done something we haven’t seen in over 20 years. In New York’s 4-3 shootout win over the Nashville Predators on Tuesday, Schaefer became the first player since the 2004-05 lockout to play all five minutes of overtime. Schaefer drew a tripping penalty on Predators forward Filip Forsberg 2 minutes and 17 seconds into the overtime period, giving him a chance to grab a breather during a stoppage in what is typically relentless 3-on-3 action. Of course, the Islanders kept Schaefer out there for the entirety of the proceeding 4-on-3 power play, and he stayed on for the remaining 43 seconds after the power play had ended to complete the full five minutes of OT. The 19-year-old blueliner even had to get on his horse to impede a potential breakaway for Forsberg after he stepped out of the penalty box. The Hamilton, Ontario native finished the game with 32 minutes and 16 seconds of ice time, clearing the next closest Islanders skater by over six minutes. Coming into Tuesday’s game, he was averaging 26 minutes and 13 seconds of ice time. Schaefer also notched an assist on Tuesday, giving him two goals and nine assists for 11 points in 12 games this season. Last season, he put up 23 goals and 36 assists for 59 points in all 82 games en route to winning the Calder Trophy as the league’s top rookie. New York, now sitting in fourth place in the Metropolitan Division with 14 points through 12 games, will finish up a three-game road trip against the Minnesota Wild on Thursday before kicking off a three-game homestand against the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.

items.title: Kent Johnson lifts Blue Jackets to OT win after Flyers rally from 3-goal deficit
items.summary: Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the game 2:22 into overtime and the Columbus Blue Jackets beat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 on Tuesday night after coughing up a three-goal lead.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the game 2:22 into overtime and the Columbus Blue Jackets beat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 on Tuesday night after coughing up a three-goal lead. Columbus scored three goals in a 2:46 span of the first period to lead 3-0 after one. Johnson set up Adam Fantilli for the first goal at 10:58 of the first period, and then deflected Zach Werenski's shot past Flyers goalie Dan Vladar at 12:54. Denton Mateychuk scored for Columbus 50 seconds later. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for his third win this season. Johnson scored the overtime winner on a two-on-none breakaway, following a give-and-go with Fantilli. It was Johnson's sixth goal of the season. Philadelphia forced overtime by outshooting Columbus 28-6 over the final two periods. Noah Cates scored his first goal of the season by poking a loose puck past Talbot, while Trevor Zegras cut the deficit to 3-2 with just under five minutes left in regulation. Zegras slid a pass to Tyson Foerster, who fired a shot on Talbot that Jamie Drysdale tipped into the net with 11 seconds remaining. Despite losing consecutive games, the Flyers have scored points in four of five games after starting the season with a franchise-record nine-game winless streak. Columbus won consecutive games for the first time this season. Blue Jackets: Continue their road trip in Carolina on Thursday. Flyers: Travel to Washington to play the Capitals on Wednesday.

items.title: Hakstol taking ASU job head-on as program investigates player’s collapse
items.body: TEMPE, Ariz. — Dave Hakstol left his job as an NHL assistant coach during the season to lead a college hockey program still reeling from the collapse of a player during an outdoor workout. Hakstol's approach in the 12 days since he took the job at Arizona State has been the same as previous stops during a career spanning more than three decades coaching in the NHL and college. “I’m aware of some of the things that some of these players are possibly dealing with, yet I make no assumptions,” Hakstol said Tuesday. “So we just kind of hit things head-on on a daily basis. And the overriding thing that these guys want, they want to be coached.” The 58-year-old left the stability of working as an assistant with the Colorado Avalanche to take over a program still investigating the collapse of defenseman Matthew Mayich during an outdoor workout on Aug. 20. Mayich is still hospitalized and is unlikely to recover from external heat stroke that reduced the flow of oxygen to his brain. Arizona State brought in former Arizona Supreme Court Chief Justice Scott Bales to lead an independent review, requesting it be completed by early December. Coach Greg Powers, who was present during the workout that caused Mayich's collapse, was initially placed on administrative leave before agreeing with ASU to leave his position when Hakstol was hired on Oct. 15. Hakstol arrived with the program in a delicate position and took a direct approach, meeting with the team and with players individually to allay any concerns. “The best thing that I can do is provide leadership for whatever the day brings; provide leadership off the ice, provide leadership, direction and coaching on the ice,” Hakstol said. “And that’s exactly what I’ve done. He was traded to Chicago after 245 games with the orange and black, unable to continue his scoring pace in the new environment as Chicago notched 46 wins as a high flying #1 ranked team. Teammates of Hall of Famers Bobby Hull and Stan Mikita , Lacroix offered 11 points in 51 games as his NHL stint came to an end at the end of the season, with the Blackhawks being dispatched in the semi-finals. Lacroix began his NHL career with the Flyers in 1967-68 and played 245 games with them over four seasons. The center led Philadelphia in points twice, finishing with 56 points (24 goals, 32 assists) in 75 games in 1968-69, and 58 points (22 goals, 36 assists) in 74 games in 1969-70. Lacroix then was traded to the Chicago Black Hawks for 1971-72 before joining the WHA with the Philadelphia Blazers the following season, when he led the league with 124 points (50 goals, 74 assists). He also played for the New York Golden Blades/Jersey Knights, San Diego Mariners, Houston Aeros and New England Whalers over his seven WHA seasons. In 1974-75, his first season with San Diego, Lacroix won his second WHA scoring title with 147 points (41 goals, 106 assists) in 78 games. He also set the professional record for assists that season; at the time, he was the only player other than Bobby Orr (102 assists for the Boston Bruins in 1970-71) who had ever reached 100 in a single season of professional hockey. The record stood until Wayne Gretzky had 109 assists for the Edmonton Oilers in 1980-81. Lacroix is the WHA all-time leader in points (798, including 251 goals), assists (547) and games played (551). Following the WHA-NHL merger in 1979, Lacroix returned to the NHL for a sixth and final season, playing for the Hartford Whalers in 1979-80 before retiring. He finished with 198 points (79 goals, 119 assists) in 325 NHL regular-season games and seven points (two goals, five assists) in 16 Stanley Cup Playoff games. Head coach Ryan Craig spoke with media, including Kirkell , after the team’s morning skate but had no updates on Hart’s injury – other than to say that he is being evaluated and Adin Hill will start in Tuesday’s game. It was not clear when Hart sustained his injury. The 28 year old has been off to a shaky start through the 2026-27 season. He boasts a 4-3-1 record and .889 save percentage through eight games so far. While below where Vegas would like him, Hart’s performances still sit higher than Hill, who has posted a 4-1-0 record and .882 save percentage. Despite those marks, Vegas ranks 10th-best in the NHL in goals-against per-game (2.92). The Golden Knights will hope Hill can fortify that standing against a Senators team averaging three goals-per-game this season. If Hart misses extended time, the Golden Knights would likely recall Carl Lindbom from the AHL’s Henderson Silver Knights. Lindbom has posted a 2-1-0 record and .940 save percentage in four games this season.

items.summary: It may seem like a no-brainer to move promising youngster Ike Howard into the top six. But Mark Spector provides a window into why it’s not that easy.
items.body: EDMONTON — Anyone who has listened to sports radio, or watched the afternoon hockey shows, has heard the pleas. “He’s a Top 6 guy! How can you call him up, then play him on the fourth line!?!” Or this one: “Give him 10 games with (fill in your No. 1 centre here) and see if he can handle it?” In Toronto, with the injury to Kirill Marchenko, they’re screaming for Gavin McKenna to get a shot on the second line with Nick Paul and William Nylander. When the Hyman injury hit, Oilers head coach Mike Babcock went with a guy who was having a good game, moving Colton Dach up into Hyman’s spot. But with a day to think about it, do you think he’d change his mind? Well, before we get into that, let’s give you a window into what a veteran coach thinks when his GM hands him a young, inexperienced, offensive player to develop. Todd McLellan had Connor McDavid as a rookie when he coached in Edmonton. Adam Proteau Partner Oct 27, 2026 9:27 PM Published Oct 27, 2026 9:27 PM The Chicago Blackhawks have been in rebuild for years now, but there's been no progress for Chicago fans to point to. Do head coach Jeff Blashill and GM Kyle Davidson have any legitimate solutions to fix this team? If one thing is true about an Original Six NHL team transitioning from a golden era to a new generation, it's that nothing is guaranteed. The Detroit Red Wings are a perfect example, as they once were the league’s gold standard, but for the past decade they've missed the Stanley Cup playoffs. In the same boat – under nearly identical circumstances as the Red Wings – are the Chicago Blackhawks . From 2010 through 2015, Chicago won three Cups, and through the eyes of most hockey observers, the Blackhawks could do no wrong. items.summary: Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart left the team’s morning skate with an undisclosed injury, and Adin Hill will start Tuesday night’s game against the Ottawa Senators.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart left the team's morning skate with an undisclosed injury, and Adin Hill will start Tuesday night's game against the Ottawa Senators. “He's in good hands,” coach Ryan Craig said. “We've got a plan here moving forward either way. We'll be ready for tonight.” Hart is 4-3-1, with a 2.76 goals-against average and an .889 save percentage, but he has shared much of the net time with Hill (4-1, 2.95, .882). Both goaltenders have dealt with injuries over the past several seasons. Hart missed nearly three months last season after injuring his left leg and then was expected to back up Hill in the playoffs. But then-coach Bruce Cassidy was fired with eight games left, and replacement John Tortorella instead put Hart in the net. Hart delivered by helping lead a late surge in the regular season before going 12-4 over the first three rounds with a 2.22 GAA and .924 save percentage. He struggled in the Stanley Cup Final against Carolina, however, becoming the first goalie to allow at least four goals in the first five games. The Hurricanes won the series in six games. Hart's presence in Vegas was a controversial topic in the hockey world and beyond. He was one of five players from the 2018 Canada world junior team who were acquitted last July of sexual assault. The NHL ruled those players were eligible to sign deals beginning Oct. 15, 2025, and to play starting Dec. 1. Hart signed a two-year, $4 million contract with the Golden Knights.

items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Activate Dante Fabbro By Brennan McClain | at October 27, 2026 2:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Columbus Blue Jackets activated defenseman Dante Fabbro from the injured reserve. Columbus had an open roster spot, so they didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move. Fabbro, 28, has been recovering from a broken hand suffered in preseason. The right-handed blueliner will return after missing the first four weeks of the regular season and the Blue Jackets’ first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign. Based on line rushes from practice, Fabbro will play on Columbus’ bottom pairing next to Erik Gudbranson . Fabbro will begin his ninth NHL season and second full season with the Blue Jackets. Columbus claimed Fabbro off waivers from the Nashville Predators around this time a few years ago. The early stages of his tenure with the Blue Jackets were promising. Fabbro typically played with Zach Werenski , allowing him to score nine goals and 26 points in 62 games with a +23 rating, averaging 21:39 of ice time per game. He also earned a 91.7% on-ice SV% at even strength, one of his career-best marks. Given his chemistry with Werenski, Columbus quickly signed Fabbro to a four-year, $16.5MM ($4.125MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, he didn’t play as well last season. Fabbro finished the 2025-26 campaign with five goals and 11 points in 74 games with a -16 rating, averaging 16:34 of ice time per game. He continued to block shots at a high rate, but nearly every offensive and defensive metric fell. Regardless, the Blue Jackets continue to inch toward a healthy defensive corps. After activating Fabbro, defenseman Ivan Provorov is the only defenseman left on the injured reserve as he continues to recover from a lower-body injury.

items.body: Paul Maurice doesn't think Winnipeg suddenly has become a bad place to play in the aftermath of the Connor Hellebuyck saga. The Florida Panthers coach, in the Manitoba capital to take on his former team, was asked about Hellebuyck's trade demand and eventual deal last week to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday. "I know the guys that play for the Winnipeg Jets ; the guys in that room love playing here. That's been true," said Maurice, who coached the Jets from 2014 to 2021. "Take a look at a guy like (Jets captain) Adam Lowry. I think sometimes, unfortunately, we have to take notice of the players that leave, but probably like you did this weekend (at the Heritage Classic), celebrate some of the great Jets that have been here, and you've got some great ones in your room." Over the years, things haven't always ended well with prominent Jets players. However, guys like Hellebuyck, Mark Scheifele and Kyle Connor did sign extensions with the small-market franchise. Maurice has maintained a deep connection to Winnipeg, saying, "If I could have one more thing, it's for the Winnipeg Jets to win the Stanley Cup," in a Sportsnet television interview on the ice after the Panthers captured their first of back-to-back titles in 2023. He was Hellebuyck's coach in Winnipeg when the goaltender broke into the league in 2015. "I don't know if it's (players) repeatedly wanting out. The 19-year-old forward took full contact during a session that lasted more than an hour. He has missed two games since Oct. 20, when he experienced a vasovagal syncope, a common cause of fainting that occurs when a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure results in reduced blood blow to the brain. "Felt pretty good," Kindel said. "Was nice to be back out there with the guys and preparing for this weekend. ... I wouldn't say it's that tough. For me, it's in the past now. It's out of my head. Can't control what happened. Just have to move forward. "That's where my head's at. Just looking to move forward now. So, I'm definitely not dwelling on anything or have anything holding me back coming into this weekend." One day after playing 18:53 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Oct. 19, Kindel fell unconscious for about 10 minutes shortly after the plane departed Salt Lake City International Airport. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Reimer made his New York Rangers debut Monday night against the Los Angeles Kings , but he was pulled after he gave up three goals on eight shots in the opening frame. The Rangers lost 6-3, and head coach Mike Sullivan pointed the blame at himself in the post-game media availability. “For (Reimer) to come in the way he has, in short order, and to go into a game like this. It’s not an easy challenge. It’s a tough challenge. I just felt the game was going, I just felt like maybe (Reimer) needs a little more preparation before we put him in that circumstance,” he said. It’s been a whirlwind two weeks for Reimer. He was signed to a professional tryout with the Hartford Wolf Pack , the Rangers’ AHL affiliate; became the oldest AHL goalie to record a shutout in nearly 20 years, then signed a one-year contract with the Rangers on Sunday. New York needed a goaltender after former Vezina Trophy winner Igor Shesterkin suffered a season-ending injury earlier this month. Including Monday’s game, Reimer has a 232-191-67 record with a .909 save percentage (SV%) and 2.88 goals against average (GAA) in 540 career games with the Rangers, Ottawa Senators , Anaheim Ducks , Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks , Carolina Hurricanes , Florida Panthers and Toronto Maple Leafs . Reimer, a native of Morweena, Man., is 5-5 with a .925 SV% and 2.70 GAA in 11 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He led the Leafs through seven games in a first-round, seven-game series against the Boston Bruins in 2013. New York is 7-6-1 with 15 points through their first 14 games of 2026-27. items.body: Register Login Oilers’ Zach Hyman Leaves Game With Injury By Brennan McClain | at October 27, 2026 8:30 am The Edmonton Oilers lost another forward to injury last night against the Detroit Red Wings. Partway through the second period, winger Zach Hyman exited prematurely after being hit by Red Wings defenseman Andreas Englund . Later in the evening, Jason Gregor of the Jason Gregor Show said Hyman is expected to miss at least a week with a concussion. Still, the Oilers haven’t specified Hyman’s injury or his potential recovery timeline. The hit didn’t appear very malicious ( video link ). The two players met at the blue line, and Englund pushed Hyman into the boards. Still, Hyman hit his head the wrong way on the plexiglass, immediately beginning to grab the back of his head and falling to the ice. Hyman has suffered multiple upper-body injuries throughout his career, but this would be his first documented concussion. Even if he only misses a week, it’s another troubling blow to the Oilers and Hyman. The 12-year veteran recently returned from an upper-body injury and had scored one goal in his first six games of the 2026-27 campaign. Edmonton should get some short-term relief in his absence, as Jason Dickinson is expected to return from a lower-body injury tomorrow. Still, the Oilers can’t catch their breath. On offense, once Dickinson returns, Hyman will join Mattias Janmark and Matthew Savoie in the press box.
